primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Mucolipidosis II alpha/beta (I-cell disease) due to GNPTAB deficiency
mechanism: GNPTAB encodes the alpha/beta subunits of N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphotransferase, which initiates mannose-6-phosphate targeting of lysosomal hydrolases in the Golgi. Loss of this enzyme causes lysosomal enzymes to be missorted and secreted extracellularly rather than delivered efficiently to lysosomes.
vignette: A 7-month-old infant has severe growth failure, coarse facial features, gingival hypertrophy, joint contractures, and skeletal abnormalities. Plasma activities of multiple lysosomal hydrolases are markedly increased, whereas cultured fibroblasts show deficient intracellular lysosomal enzyme activity. Sequencing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in GNPTAB.
lead: Which of the following cellular processes is most directly impaired in this disorder?
correct: Golgi tagging of lysosomal hydrolases for mannose-6-phosphate-dependent trafficking to lysosomes
distractors: Binding of lysosomal hydrolases to the mannose-6-phosphate receptor after normal phosphorylation
Acidification of the lysosomal lumen by the vacuolar H+-ATPase
Fusion of autophagosomes with lysosomes during macroautophagy
Proteolytic cleavage of lysosomal proenzymes after they reach the lysosomal compartment
distractor_notes: A receptor-binding defect could also disturb lysosomal targeting, but mucolipidosis II from GNPTAB loss is caused upstream by failure of the phosphotransferase-mediated tagging step.
Lysosomal acidification defects impair enzyme function after delivery; they do not explain secretion of many hydrolases into plasma due to missorting in the Golgi.
Autophagosome-lysosome fusion defects affect autophagic degradation but are not the primary GNPTAB trafficking lesion.
Defective proenzyme processing would occur after lysosomal delivery and would not produce the characteristic broad extracellular elevation of lysosomal hydrolases.
key_expl: Mucolipidosis II alpha/beta is a GNPTAB-related lysosomal trafficking disorder. GNPTAB encodes N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphotransferase alpha/beta subunits. Loss of phosphotransferase activity prevents appropriate Golgi targeting modification of lysosomal hydrolases, causing missorting and extracellular secretion rather than normal lysosomal delivery. This explains high plasma hydrolase activity despite intracellular lysosomal deficiency.
objective: Explain mucolipidosis II as GNPTAB-dependent failure of mannose-6-phosphate targeting of lysosomal enzymes in the Golgi.
